newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU extends Russia textiles deal to April 1997.
newsitem.headline: EU extends Russia textiles deal to April 1997.

text.p: The European Commission extended by three months on Friday an existing textiles accord with Russia and ended import quota restrictions on five product types including skirts, dresses and tracksuits, a statement said.
The decision extends this year's textiles agreement between the European Union and Russia until next April.
"This temporary step is intended as a first step towards further, and eventually complete, liberalisation," the statement said.

In addition to new duty-free status for the five product categories, which also include yarns, fabrics and clothing accessories, EU quotas on the 34 other Russian product categories will increase by 15 percent.
Bilateral discussions continue between the Commission and Moscow aimed at the elimination over the next years of quotas on all imports of Russian textiles and clothing.
"The security that such an agreement will bring will benefit both Russian industry and EU importers," the statement said.
Commission figures put total Russian exports of textiles and clothing to the EU at 26,789 tonnes in 1995, with the five quotas categories covered by Friday's announcement accounting for 3,297 tonnes.
